To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount of digestive enzymes used in gastrointestinal in vivo digestion can affect mineral solubility and uptake in Caco-2 model.
the amount of enzymes used in the digestion process has a great effect on the solubility of minerals from IFs.
the amount of enzymes used in in vitro digestion can affect the solubility of minerals from infant formulas and their uptake by Caco- 2 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of the amounts of enzymes used in gastrointestinal digestion upon the mineral solubility and mineral absorption in Caco-2 intestinal cells.
the effect of enzyme amounts in gastrointestinal digestion upon the soluble contents and Caco- 2 cell uptake of minerals from IFs.
the importance of the enzyme amounts used for gastrointestinal in vitro digestion in mineral bioavailability studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amounts of enzymes used in gastrointestinal digestion affect the solubility, and hence the Caco-2 uptake, of calcium, iron or zinc from IFs.
the mineral uptake by Caco- 2 cells is affected by the enzyme digestion, which is a complex process, and the results obtained in this study are in agreement with those reported in previous studies.
enzyme amounts used in in vitro gastrointestinal digestion should be optimized in relation to the mineral of interest and the IF under study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of different enzyme amounts can affect the solubility of minerals and the uptake of minerals by Caco- 2 cells, but the relationship between solubilization and mineral absorption is not clear.
the mineral solubilities and Caco- 2 cell uptakes are influenced by the enzyme amounts in the gastrointestinal digestion.
mineral solubility in IFs is not a predictor of the mineral absorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mineral uptake by Caco- 2 cells depends on the amount of enzyme used in gastrointestinal digestion, but it is not related with solubility.
the amount of enzymes used in gastrointestinal in-vitro digestion can affect mineral solubility and mineral absorption by Caco- 2 cells.
the amount of enzymes used for gastrointestinal digestion can affect the mineral solubility and uptake by Caco- 2 cells.
